meta.purpose: Second-domain evaluation corpus, built to the same rigor as the synthetic-domain benchmark (T1-T5 tiers, independently-authored gold, house_vocab + out_of_range supplementary tiers).
meta.authoring_note: Questions are phrased as an HR analyst would ask, NOT as engine-shaped goal specs. The 'intent' field is the unambiguous specification the INDEPENDENT gold script (evidence/gold/build_gold_employee.py) implements (plain pandas, zero imports from the engine). T5 thresholds were verified against the real augmented probe_domain/employees.pkl data before being finalized, not guessed -- see this session's threshold-verification work.
meta.corpus_size_note: 91 queries, not 93: two originally-drafted house_vocab queries ('typical bonus for managers' and 'way more than market rate') were DROPPED after verification against real data found them genuinely undefined -- 'managers' splits into two non-overlapping populations with materially different answers (Role==Manager: 29 people, constant $19,500 bonus; generic supervisory staff: 98 people spanning all 4 roles, mean $25,469), and 'way more than market rate' has no natural gap in the salary_variance distribution to anchor a threshold on. This mirrors eval_corpus.json's own precedent of dropping hv_01/hv_04 for an undefined term ('exposure'). On 2026-10-01 oor_03 ('Compare our salaries to industry benchmarks.') was dropped from scoring (decision D11): it has a defensible answering reading (Market Rate, which schema.json describes as the 'External market benchmark salary for the employee's role'), so a refusal is not the only correct behaviour. 90 queries; out_of_range is 9.
